result.headline: No published result resolves or partially resolves Wilhelm–Heinrich uniqueness (open in Boros–Hofbauer 2023; nothing later found), and no existing uniqueness theorem applies: Massera-, Zhang-, concave-return-map and curvature-Dulac hypotheses were checked and fail. The only precedent, Jones' conjecture, needed asymptotics plus computer-assisted proof. By-product proved here: every projected cycle is strictly star-shaped and convex, giving exact formulas lambda_c = -<pK/S*> = -<pW/V>.

claims.statement: The cycle count above Hopf is still open. It is stated open in Smith 2012 (after Thm 1.1) and Boros–Hofbauer 2023 (after Thm 13). Citation graphs of both papers and of Wilhelm–Heinrich 1995/96 (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar), arXiv listings and web searches to 2026-10-03 show no later result. A 2025 MATCH paper citing Smith concerns the Willamowski–Rössler system, not this one.

For mu=1 the system is exactly the linear-chain form of the strong-kernel delayed logistic equation (Ruan survey eq. 9.11). The distributed-delay literature (Ruan Thms 7–9; Cushing, MacDonald) gives global stability for the weak kernel and only local Hopf existence/stability for the strong kernel. No uniqueness or global orbital-stability theorem for gamma/Erlang-kernel periodic solutions was found.

Jones' conjecture was proved in three regimes: Xie (alpha>=5.67: every slowly oscillating periodic solution is stable, and stable-for-all implies unique); Jaquette–Lessard–Mischaikow ([1.9,6.0]: interval bounding functions for all periodic solutions plus Floquet bounds); Jaquette ((pi/2,1.9]: Fourier-space branch-and-bound) with van den Berg–Jaquette's explicit Hopf neighbourhood. Stability arguments are stated to be infeasible near Hopf.

No general uniqueness theorem exists for periodic orbits of 3-D competitive or negative cyclic feedback systems with smooth nonlinearity; Katz–Giordano–Margaliot (JDE 2025) list it as open. Known results need step or piecewise-linear nonlinearities (Glass–Pasternack, Farcot–Gouzé), steep-Hill regimes (Hastings 1977) or relaxation asymptotics. The 1981 neuron-model paper is Bingxi Li, Nonlinear Anal. 5:13–19; its hypotheses were not obtainable.

On every nonconstant cycle S*=p^2-Up'>0 and V=p'^2-pp''>0: the (U,p) projection is strictly star-shaped about E and strictly convex. Identities S*'=(eta-mu)S*+pK and V'=(eta-mu)V+pW give lambda_c=-<pK/S*>=-<pW/V>, and the rising-arc integral of eta-mu is below 2log r, the falling-arc integral above -2log r, r=(y_crest-k)/(k-y_trough). Uses v2.0 Prop 2.2, Cor 3.2, Lemma 3.3, Thm 4.1.

Planar uniqueness theorems do not apply to the reduced flow. Sabatini–Villari radial angular monotonicity equals -vK; the Gasull–Giacomini curvature Dulac defect equals pW; Sabatini's star-shapedness function takes both signs on computed cycles (about -0.36 to 1.1). Zhang-type theorems need a separable Liénard form; the formal mu->0 Liénard truncation satisfies Zhang's condition but has no cycle (first-order Melnikov function is strictly positive).

claims.statement: H. L. Smith's 1986 monotone-concave fixed-point theorem does not apply to the crest return map in power charts: monotonicity held at all 243 tested section points, but the concavity hypothesis failed in 12–34% of ordered comparisons for every chart tried. Its necessary consequence Mv<=v held on 24 cycles (rho>=1.02) but fails near Hopf unless a=(mu^2+4mu+1)/(mu^2+6mu+1)-(1-b)/(1+mu).

Smith 2012 proved below-Hopf global stability with the Li–Muldowney second-compound criterion, weights diag((1-2e)/x,(1-e)/x,-1/k5), Lozinskii measure max{...,x/(1-2e)-(k3+k5)} and <x>=k. This is brief item (e) with phi=1; above Hopf a state-dependent weight is required. Gasull–Giacomini's extended Bendixson–Dulac theorem is the published form of brief item (d). No brief item was contradicted.

result.obstruction: The nonlinearity e^U-1 is sublinear on one side of the equilibrium and superlinear on the other, and the effective damping mu-eta is monotone through the equilibrium instead of extremal there. Every structural uniqueness theorem located needs two-sided sublinearity or concavity (Cao, Krasnosel'skii, H. L. Smith), a separable Liénard form (Zhang), a damping critical point at the equilibrium (Massera, Sabatini), a step-like nonlinearity, or a small parameter. Concretely, every Dulac defect computed is a positive convexity gauge times the sign-changing factor p (-vK, pW), and the crest map is monotone but not concave. For the same nonlinearity with a pure delay (Wright's equation) uniqueness took 57 years and was closed only by large-parameter asymptotics plus computer-assisted proof. Several potentially relevant papers (Li 1981, Dai 1979, R. A. Smith 1987) were paywalled, so their hypotheses are unverified.
result.best_next_step: Exploit the new gauge family: for periodic phi, S=p*phi'-p'*phi obeys S'=(eta-mu)S+p*L2[phi]; seek phi, or a non-diagonal Li–Muldowney weight using the two new zero-mean log-derivatives of S* and V, that removes the factor p. In parallel plan a Jones-type programme: explicit Hopf collar (van den Berg–Lessard–Queirolo), validated crest map on compact parameter boxes, large-rho asymptotics, separate mu->0 analysis.

result.headline: No second cycle and no lambda_c >= 0 anywhere: 300 grid cycles (mu 0.002..1, rho-1 from 1e-3 to 199), 827 branch points, 240 random points (mu 1e-3..1e3, rho <= 285). log m_t is strictly decreasing in rho. Survivors: S1, S4. Refuted: S2 (all six coordinates), S3b, S5 one-signedness; S3a fails on the crest side for mu in about [0.7,1.5], rho >= 4.5. All floating point, no proofs.

claims.statement: Grid of 12 mu x 25 rho: all 300 cycles found, every lambda_c < 0 (max -1.93e-6 at mu=0.002, rho-1=1e-3; stable to 10 digits at rtol 1e-10..1e-13). log m_t is strictly decreasing in rho at each mu; rho(h) is strictly increasing along every amplitude branch (no fold). |log m_t| >= 0.548 x the Hopf-linear value everywhere; m_t > 0.999 only for rho-1 < 0.0035.

Hunt at 240 random points: 239,103 return-map pairs on the attractor with zero wrong-sign displacements (exactly one diagonal crossing); 1673 long runs from W^u(E), far-outside and random 3-D starts, none converging elsewhere (25 not finished: slow near Hopf or too expensive); 2868 Newton starts, zero new fixed points. One point failed in direct coordinates and was redone at the reciprocal rate.

S1 survives: at 62/62 parameter points (mu 0.002..500, rho-1 0.003..33) the one-turn mean of eta-mu decreases turn by turn along W^u(E), and is strictly decreasing in crest amplitude inside (62/62) and outside (31/31) the cycle. Near Hopf at small mu the turn-by-turn differences are at round-off level. The one-turn integral is not monotone.

S2 refuted in all six coordinates. y-k, e^U-1, sqrt(K), sqrt(W): the return map is convex near E at all 62 points. U and Lambda_E: concave at 49 and 43 of 62, failing for extreme rate ratios with larger rho. Even phi(U)/U is not decreasing: at mu=0.0027, rho=5.02, log(phi(U)/U) is 0.287 at E, 0.220 at 0.25U*, 0.245 at 0.54U*.

S3a refuted on the crest side: at mu=1, rho=5 the ratio (mu-zeta)/(k(e^U-1)) on the attractor section has slope -0.135 at the cycle (finite differences, three tolerances). It fails for mu in about [0.7,1.5] with rho >= 4.5 to 8; passes on the trough side (62/62) and for mu <= 0.5 or >= 2 up to rho=10. S3b (fixed Lienard s) fails at 62/62.

S4 survives: D^2h is strictly positive definite at all reliably computed attractor points (62/62; eigenvalue ratio 2.5e-12 to 0.10), and all 300 projected cycles are convex in (U,p). Caveat (standard node argument, not proved here): h is expected to be C^2 at the cycle only if |lambda_c| <= (1+mu)/3; the pull-back variation fails to converge at mu=1, rho=21.

S5/S6: K-(zeta-mu)chi(U) is positive on the disc only at smaller rho (174/300 cycles); a negative patch on the downstroke appears from rho-1 of about 0.7 to 2. zeta/eta <= 1 on part of every cycle and > 1 on another; x/zeta, zeta/eta+mu, k(Ue^U-e^U+1)/K, xp^2/W minus A all change sign on every cycle; their means equal lambda_c to 6 digits.

mu->0 at fixed rho is a relaxation limit, not near-neutral: m_t -> m_0(rho) in (0,1), T ~ S*(rho)/mu. A formal limit return map built from the pulse x'=px, p'=-y, y'=x-y matches the full system with O(mu) error for rho 1.03..200 (rho=1.5: -0.38688 at mu=5e-4 vs -0.38593) and has a unique fixed point for rho in (1.0002,320). The Hamiltonian window is rho-1=O(mu).

result.obstruction: No obstruction to the conjecture was found; this lane produces evidence, not proof. The obstructions are to proof strategies. Return-map concavity or star-shapedness fails structurally at small min(mu,1/mu): the map has a quasi-harmonic regime near E and a pulse-relaxation regime further out, and log(phi(U)/U) rises between them. Zhang-type f/g monotonicity is false over the disc at every tested parameter and false on the section near mu=1 at larger rho. Every pointwise candidate in S5/S6 changes sign. Limits of the evidence: floating point only; mu in [1e-3,1e3], rho <= 300; outside the cycle the return map is only defined post-transient; Hessian tests for mu > 1 cover only the crest half of the disc; isolas beyond U*+6 or thinner than the scan spacing would be missed.
result.best_next_step: Attack S1 in amplitude form: the one-turn mean of eta-mu strictly decreasing in crest amplitude on the attractor disc. Given brief item (b), it implies uniqueness, and it passed every test including the parameter sets that break S2. In parallel, treat mu->0 as a model problem: prove the limit function Lambda(p) is increasing, a parameter-free property of the pulse scattering map G.

result.obstruction: Every Dulac candidate reduces to one missing inequality. For state-function Lambda the residual is R = E(z) - p*K/V, and richer Lambda (using eta, zeta, K, W) are functions of (z, K/V) as well. R <= 0 therefore needs an upper bound on K/V (equivalently on eta) on the descending half p<0, above all just after the crest (p<0, p'<0), where eta > mu on all computed cycles. Convexity (supporting planes, K>0, W>0) bounds K/V only from below there, because the projected cycle is convex. The available dynamic upper bounds (zeta < y; eta < lambda-p for mu <= 1/2) are O(1/r) at E instead of O(1), so they cannot reproduce the first Lyapunov coefficient near Hopf. Numerically a Dulac function exists, but only with about 26 parameter-specific coefficients and no visible closed form.

result.headline: No proof of the conjecture and no counter-evidence (55 cycles, all attracting). New proved theorem: every cycle's (U,p)-projection is strictly convex and strictly star-shaped about E (S1 = p^2 - U p' > 0, S4 = p'^2 - p p'' > 0), with exact formulas lambda_c = -<pK/S1> = -<pW/S4>. Stability therefore reduces to one explicit upper bound for eta on the falling arc. Explicit state-function certificates are tightly constrained and none tested gives a provable inequality.

claims.statement: Theorem R. On every cycle S1 = p^2 - U p' > 0 and S4 = p'^2 - p p'' > 0; S1' = (eta-mu)S1 + pK, S4' = (eta-mu)S4 + pW. Hence the (U,p)-projection is strictly star-shaped about E and strictly convex, and lambda_c = -<pK/S1> = -<pW/S4> = -<p(K+c zeta)/(p^2 - p'(U+c))> for 0 <= c < |U_min|. Formulas agree with <eta>-mu to 6 digits on 55 cycles.

Proposition T. For two nested cycles with polar radii R_1 < R_2 about E: d/dtheta log(R_2/R_1) = sin(theta)(m_2-m_1)/(sigma_1 sigma_2), m_i = (y_i-k)/R_i, m_2 > m_1, sigma_i = S1/R_i^2 > 0. So R_2/R_1 increases on (0,pi), decreases on (pi,2pi): trough-depth ratio > every radial ratio > crest-height ratio > 1. No contradiction derived from it.

Lemma A0. A supersolution omega = phi(1,eta~,zeta~) gives lambda_c <= -<min(mu-eta~, Dlog eta~ + 1 - zeta~/eta~, Dlog zeta~ + A - x/zeta~)>; the scalar factor phi drops out; equality at the true (eta,zeta). For log-linear families (log eta~, log zeta~ linear in fixed state features) the objective is concave in the exponents, so family existence is a convex programme.

Lemma A1 (first-order rigidity). Under C^1 expansions in the Hopf amplitude, any certificate direction with nonnegative score must equal (mu,mu) at order 0 and the true first-order pair at order eps: eta~ = mu + (mu A/D)U - (2mu/D)p, zeta~ = mu + (mu(mu^2+4mu+1)/D)U - (mu A/D)p, D = mu^2+6mu+1. Hence omega^Y, omega^c, radial and constant directions are dead near Hopf.

Target B. Brief identity 3(f) holds in quantitative form: lambda_c = <a^ x(lambda-A-2p)>/<c^ P + b^ y + a^ x>, chi(gamma) = <x a^>/<a^>, lambda_c = <beta>-A with beta = b/a. For mu <= 1: beta > 1 and c/a > (1-mu)beta pointwise. Ratio check 1.000000 on 54 of 55 cycles (0.9989 on the stiffest). The sign itself is not proved.

Target A family verdicts (averaged criterion, per-cycle concave optimum over 55 cycles): omega^Y, omega^c, radial, K<-Lambda_E, exp-linear: negative on all cycles. Monomials x^a Z^b Y^c: negative near Hopf for mu <= 0.2 (ratio -0.41 at mu=0.05). Adding Lambda_E: still negative at mu <= 0.1 near Hopf. Monomials in X,Z,Y,Z*: positive on all 55 (0.27 to 0.985 of -lambda_c).

The X,Z,Y,Z* monomial family needs k-dependent exponents: no common-exponent certificate found over rho in [1.001,10] (best min-ratio -0.46 to -15), though one exists on [2,10] for mu <= 0.5. Pointwise on-cycle certificates in the family were found only near Hopf (rho <= 1.03 to 1.1) and not for rho >= 1.3; these pointwise negatives are solver lower bounds, not refutations.

Scalar reduction: the true (eta,zeta) lies on the explicit line zeta p - eta p' = y'; with eta = (S2 - pK)/S1, K solves the scalar Riccati K' = kG1(U) - (1+S2/S1)K + (p/S1)K^2, S2/S1 = mu + (log S1)'. Target C becomes <pK/S1> > 0. Also S1 = Q_E + U Lambda_E and <(p - alpha U)Lambda_E/Q_E> = alpha exactly.

result.obstruction: Three linked obstructions. (1) First-order rigidity: any explicit certificate must reproduce the 2-jet of W^u(E) at Hopf exactly, leaving only O(eps^2) slack; the one parameter-free first-order-exact trial (K replaced by Lambda_E) has the wrong second-order balance (score -2 to -100 times |lambda_c|). (2) The supersolution bound is an average of a minimum along an unknown cycle; only total derivatives have known averages, so an averaged certificate is not a proof, and pointwise on-cycle monomial certificates were not found beyond rho about 1.3. (3) Sign of p: every radial identity reads (log s)' = eta - mu + pN/s with N > 0, an upper bound for eta on the rising arc but a lower bound on the falling arc, where every known pointwise constraint also bounds eta from below. Targets B and C yield identities only; the sign sits in a phase lag.

result.headline: Job 1 proved in full: the global attractor is a convex C^1 graph y=h(U,p) over the closed Jordan domain bounded by the outermost projected cycle, with grad h=(zeta,-eta), planar divergence eta-mu, and uniqueness equivalent (up to lambda_c=0) to lambda_c<0 on every cycle. Proof is self-contained on classical theorems only. Job 2 (uniqueness) not proved: natural pointwise Zhang/Massera/Dulac/rotation candidates are numerically refuted; crest return-map concavity is supported but unproved.

claims.statement: Theorem A (A1-A5), all mu,k>0: compact connected global attractor A = all log-bounded entire orbits; along each a unique nonnegative entire Riccati solution (eta,zeta), uniformly bounded, continuous on A; strict supporting planes between any two points of A; pi|A injective; A = graph of h=H|_D, H convex; h is C^1 on int D with grad h=(zeta,-eta); reduced field (v,k-mu v-h) has divergence eta-mu.

Theorem A (A6-A7), k>k_H: A meets E+C_+ and E+C_- only at E; no log-bounded entire orbit other than E converges to E forwards; W^u(E) lies in A; every other orbit in A has a cycle as omega-limit; the crest set is compact; D is exactly the closed Jordan domain bounded by the outermost projected cycle.

Theorem A (A8): planar multiplier of each cycle equals m_t; innermost and outermost cycles have lambda_c<=0; if every cycle has lambda_c<0 the cycle is unique; if all cycles are hyperbolic their number is odd with alternating stability; Dulac form: D Lambda+eta-mu<=0 (not a.e. zero) on all cycles implies a unique attracting cycle.

Conditional criterion (Prop 8.1): on the crest half-axis R_1'(u)=g(u)exp(iota(u))/g(R_1 u), g(u)=h(u,0)-k; in the energy coordinate the return map has derivative exp(iota), iota the turn integral of eta-mu. If iota is strictly decreasing, or R_1(u)/u is strictly decreasing, the cycle is unique.

The crest turn integral iota is strictly decreasing and R_1 is concave and sublinear in U at all 14 tested (mu,rho) pairs. The trough-section analogue is false, and R_1 is not concave in x-k or y-k. The exact derivative formula for iota has a sign-changing integrand.

Pointwise candidates fail on the attractor disc: generalised Zhang condition d/dU(P_U/g)<=0 violated on 2-18% of points (34-60% in the (y,m) plane); Massera weights 1/(X^xi) in 12 charts have wrong sign on 21-53%; 11 explicit Dulac candidates and a 14-function LP span fail; the Lienard-plane family is not rotated in k.

Exact identity: F(theta q)^F(q) = -v[theta(H(q)-k)+k-H(theta q)], bracket >=0 by convexity. So radial scaling in (U,p) is crossed outward where p>0 and inward where p<0. In 3D, for nu=(U,p,y-k): D omega - C omega = k(Ue^U-e^U+1)(0,p,p').

LP lead: a state-explicit compound supersolution omega=conj(f^nu), nu = radial plus degree-2 correction in (U,p,y-k,e^U-1), exists on sampled attractor points and validates out of sample at (mu,rho)=(1,1.02),(1,1.1),(1,1.5),(0.3,1.1),(0.3,1.5); it overfits or is infeasible at larger rho and at mu=0.1, 3, 10. Degree 1 is infeasible.

result.obstruction: Uniqueness on the reduced planar system was not proved. The only structure h keeps beyond its first-order PDE is convexity, and every comparison convexity yields reverses with the sign of p after projection: scaled orbit arcs are crossed outward in the upper half-plane and inward in the lower (exact identity). Zhang, Massera and Dulac criteria need a one-signed quantity on an annulus; every natural pointwise candidate tested changes sign on 20-60% of the disc. What holds numerically is an integrated, section-specific statement (crest return map concave in U; false on the trough section and in x or y coordinates) whose derivative has a sign-changing integrand. Rotation in k, even if true, only makes the amplitude curve single-valued and allows fold pairs. A proof must exploit crest/trough asymmetry of the exponential, not convexity of h alone.

result.headline: The sign of lambda_c was not obtained. Proved instead a new structural theorem for every cycle: the weak adjoint is Psi = e^{At} z' x e_s; its three components each have exactly two zeros, interlacing the six extrema; and the strong-stable plane span{z'(t), e_s(t)} strictly supports the whole cycle, E and all nested inner cycles. No counter-evidence: all 23 computed cycles are attracting.

claims.statement: Dual supporting planes: for every cycle, all t and all s not 0 mod T, det(z(t+s)-z(t), z'(t), e_s(t)) < 0, det(E-z(t), z'(t), e_s(t)) < 0 and det(z''(t), z'(t), e_s(t)) < 0, where e_s=(a,-b,-c), a,b,c>0, is the strong-stable Floquet vector. The first inequality also holds for points of any cycle nested inside.

Twelve-event order: each component of the weak adjoint Psi has exactly two simple zeros per period, ordered trough < Psi2 up < Zmin < Psi1 up < p-max < Psi3 up (t2) < crest < Psi2 down < Zmax < Psi1 down < p-min < Psi3 down (t1). Psi3 is proportional to -(p' + r p), r=b/a; Psi>0 at crest, Psi<0 at trough.

Rank-one window identity: for every T-periodic phi, the integral over [t1,t1+T] of Psi3*L3[phi] equals (e^{-lambda_c T}-1)|Psi2(t1)|(phi'+r phi)(t1). Hence lambda_c<0 iff window-integral of Psi3*x >0 iff that of Psi3*x*p^2 <0 iff that of Psi3*(1-e^U+Ue^U) <0. All periodic test functions carry the same single unknown sign.

Strong-stable ratios r=b/a, s=c/a satisfy r'=r^2-mu r-s, s'=sr-s-x, r>max(1,mu), s>0, equivalently r''+(A-3r)r'+r(r-1)(r-mu)=x with <r>=1+<eta>. The conjecture is equivalent to <r><A for this positive periodic solution (time-reversed mirror of the eta equation).

The crest return map P is entrywise monotone (DP>0) at every point of R={p=0, x>=y>k}, not only at cycles, and maps R into its interior. At a cycle crest the Perron eigenvector of DP is exactly (1, zeta(crest)).

P is not radially sublinear about E (violated at 5 to 95 of 98 test pairs; near Hopf the second component of Mv<=v fails at O(h) for the radial vector) and not order-concave in (U,y). The wedges (z-E)^z' and z'^z'' are not componentwise positive. (eta-mu)^2<4 zeta fails for rho>=1.3.

On 15 cycles (mu 0.05 to 4, rho 1.01 to 5): J0=<a^(p'+rp)> = -<Psi3> > 0 (k would be a regular parameter at a neutral cycle) and <Psi3 x nu^2> > 0; the (U,p) projection is strictly convex and star-shaped; the weak Floquet vector e_t shows the analogous zero interlacing.

Fold-direction reduction: the conjecture follows if, at every neutral cycle, the weak components of dP/dk and of D^2P along the Perron direction have the same sign (the first neutral event on a fixed-mu path must be a birth fold or degenerate, which needs opposite signs). Jordan-block corrections at the unit multiplier are not worked out.

result.obstruction: Pairing the weak adjoint with any periodic test function gives one and the same rank-one identity: the sign of lambda_c equals the sign of a crest-arc minus trough-arc integral of |Psi3| against a nonnegative weight, and the dominant arc differs between weights (x versus x p^2, g(U), chord weights). A sign proof needs a test function whose L3-image changes sign exactly at the two phases t1, t2 where the projected strong-stable direction is tangent to the projected cycle; these are defined through the non-explicit ratio r=-a'/a. Convexity and monotonicity of the backward flow live in the cone whose Perron direction is e_s, so their first-order consequences are dominated by the factor e^{gamma T}-1 and only bound |1/m_t - 1|. Near Hopf the relevant integrals are O(h^4) with cancellation at O(h^3), and any Krasnoselskii scaling must match zeta(crest) to O(h^2).

Imports v2.0 facts: positive adjoint, Lambda_E>0 and cone exclusion, one crest/trough, T>2pi/sqrt(mu), state box.

Key foothold (new): on every cycle the positive lobe {U>0} lasts T_+ < pi/omega (omega = imaginary part of the unstable eigenvalue of E), by a Sturm argument from Lambda_E>0. With T>2pi/sqrt(mu) the negative lobe lasts > 2pi - pi/omega_0(k), which for k>=1000 forces p_k >= 0.374 k via a four-duration pigeonhole.

Spike mass lemma: M_+ = integral over {U>0} of (x-k) satisfies M_+(M_+ + mu P_1) >= (1/4)p_k^2[(1/2)p_k^2 - 2 mu P_1 H] - p_k k/sqrt2, hence T_- > M_+/k >= p_k^2 sqrt(1-delta)/(sqrt8 k) - 1/2; a quasi-convexity bootstrap then gives T_- > 0.1833 lambda/mu and p_k >= 0.819 lambda.

Linear estimate: if x<=c0=(mu-nu)(1-nu)(A-nu) outside an interval of length tau_c per period, then (<eta>-mu)T <= -nu(T-tau_c)+(s-mu)tau_c+kT/s^2+log(1+alpha s+beta s^2) for all s>=sqrt2 (Lyapunov a+alpha b+beta c on the trough, max(s^2 a, s b, c) on the crest, for the cooperative system a'=-mu a+b, b'=-b+c, c'=-Ac+xa).

Corollaries: uniqueness and attraction of all positive orbits off W^s(E) for mu<=1, k>=1000 (depends on Smith 2012 convergence theorem as quoted in v2.0); for mu>=1 the same when k>=1000 mu^3, i.e. rho >= 1000/(m(1+m)), m=min(mu,1/mu). Only cycles and multipliers are transported by the symmetry; positive domains do NOT correspond.

All numerical constants and scalar side conditions of the proof hold at K0=1000 (mpmath 40 digits, 60+ checks); all lemma inequalities hold on 11 computed cycles; derivation steps hold on 365 random non-periodic segments; Stage-1/2 lemmas hold on random non-periodic lobes.

Empirical asymptotics of the computed cycle: T ~ 1.305 lambda/mu, spike mass M_+ ~ 1.305 p_k^2, p_k/lambda -> 1, integral of x^(1/3) over the crest ~ 4.6, integral of eta over a period grows only like log(lambda).

result.headline: The first-order Melnikov premise is false: M(h) = (1−rho)·oint U'^2 has no zero. The Hamiltonian regime is the thin wedge rho−1 = r·eps^2 (eps = sqrt(mu)/(1+mu)), selected at third order by r = (2/3)<p^4>/<p^2>. Monotonicity of that selection function is proved (derivative ≥ 4/5), and a local uniqueness theorem for small mu follows. Global uniqueness is not proved, even for small mu. At fixed rho the limit is a relaxation oscillation. PROGRAM.md written.

claims.statement: Lane-prompt claim that M(h) = oint(U'^2 − U''^2) dtau has exactly one positive zero for rho>1 (monotone ratio oint U'^2 / oint (e^U−1)^2) is false. On every Toda level oint e^U U'^2 = oint U'^2, so M(h) = (1−rho)·oint U'^2 < 0 and the ratio is the constant rho. On true cycles at fixed rho the crest energy diverges like c(rho)/mu.

Theorem A: for any strictly convex potential (in particular e^U−U−1), on the level H0=h, <P^4> ≤ (9/5)<P^2>^2. Hence Rsel(h) = (2/3)<P^4>/<P^2> has Rsel' ≥ 4/5 and is a bijection of (0,∞). The third-order selection equation r = Rsel(h), with rho = 1 + r·eps^2, has exactly one root h*(r) ≤ 5r/4, simple, with the attracting sign.

Exact identities on every cycle at all parameters (tau-time, P=U', Q=U''): <Q^2> = <P^2> = rho<e^U P^2>, and (rho−1)<P^2> = eps^2[(<P^4> − 3<Q^2 P^2>)/rho − <Q^3> + 2(1−1/rho)(<Q'^2> − <Q^2>)]. Checked to 1e-11 on 8 computed cycles.

Theorem C (uses Fenichel's theorem as a cited input; mu0 not explicit): for r in a compact subset of (0,∞), rho = 1 + r·eps^2 and mu < mu0, exactly one cycle has projection (U, U_tau) inside a fixed energy ball {H0 ≤ h_b}, h_b > h*(r). It is hyperbolic attracting with log m_t = −eps^3·J0(h*)·Rsel'(h*) + O(eps^4). Local in phase space, not global uniqueness.

Third-order prediction against true cycles (amplitude-fixed shooting, mu from 3e-2 to 1e-4, amplitudes 0.3 to 3): (rho−1)/eps^2 matches Rsel(h) within 4e-4 and log m_t/eps^3 matches −J0·Rsel' within 8e-4 at mu = 1e-4 for amplitudes up to 1; errors scale like eps^2 and grow with amplitude.

Fixed rho>1, mu→0 is a relaxation regime: a universal pulse map S of v'''+v''+e^v=0 (S(1)=2 exactly) composed with an explicit slow return. The singular 1-D map has one fixed point for each rho in {1.02, 1.1, 1.5, 3, 8}, reproduces m_t, mu·T and mu·U_min of true cycles to 3 digits, and its branch rho = Lambda(q) is increasing on a 33-point grid.

Global uniqueness in the wedge rho−1 ≤ r2·eps^2, small mu, would follow from Theorem C plus: no non-attracting cycle leaves {H0 ≤ h_b}. Non-attracting cycles satisfy <(eta−mu)^2> ≤ r·mu^2/2 and three exact formulas (proved, checked to 1e-8) that forbid spikes; closing the argument needs a-priori bounds T ≤ C/mu and p ≥ −C for arbitrary cycles, which are unproved.

Computer-assisted core (mu in [0.05,1], rho ≤ 20, outside the collar (rho−1)/eps^2 ≤ 0.2): idealised count 7e3 return-map box evaluations, realistic bracket 1e5–1e8. A Taylor-model enclosure over a full period works for boxes of half-width 1e-3 (30–190 steps, 1–10 s each in TaylorModels.jl; 10 ms assumed for CAPD, unmeasured). Small-mu wedge and large gain still need analytic theorems.

result.obstruction: The Hamiltonian picture holds only in the thin wedge rho−1 = O(mu) and only at bounded energy. Theorem C is local: nothing proved excludes an extra large non-attracting cycle (crest energy between h_b and about 2/mu) for small mu. Closing this needs either third-order averaging uniform on an unbounded energy range plus the relaxation regime, or two a-priori estimates for arbitrary cycles (period ≤ C/mu, p ≥ −C) to run the variance-window argument; neither is proved. The Hopf end r→0 is only outlined. At fixed rho>1 the small-mu limit is a relaxation oscillation with no theorem; monotonicity of Lambda is numerical only. For the full program the compact core is cheap, but the non-compact end mu→0 (two singular regimes, their matching zone, and the corner rho→∞), an explicit large-gain threshold and an explicit Hopf collar are all missing analytic pieces.
result.best_next_step: Prove the two a-priori estimates (period ≤ C/mu, p ≥ −C) for arbitrary cycles with rho−1 ≤ r2·eps^2, then make the spike inequality of NOTES §4.2b rigorous; with Theorem C and the Hopf-end outline this gives global uniqueness in the small-mu Hopf wedge. In parallel, prototype the crest-section branch-and-bound at mu=1, rho in [1.05,20] with a CAPD-class integrator to calibrate the box-count overhead.

result.headline: No proof and no counterevidence. New: (i) a rigorous Hölder sandwich <x^{1/3}>^3 < gamma(gamma-1)(gamma-mu) < k, sharpening brief 3(g); (ii) exact Lotka-Volterra and second-order-Riccati (forced Liénard) forms; (iii) numerical evidence that the 1-D crest return map on the attractor is concave with P1(u)/u strictly decreasing in u=U_crest, which would give uniqueness if proved. Nine first-principles routes were tried; each collapses to the supersolution/Dulac problem or dies for a stated reason.

claims.statement: On every nonconstant cycle, <x^{1/3}>^3 < gamma(gamma-1)(gamma-mu) < k with gamma = 1+<eta>. Hence every attracting or neutral cycle has <e^{U/3}> < rho^{-1/3}; this implies and strengthens brief 3(g). Proof: Hölder on eta, zeta/eta, x/zeta, whose means are gamma-1, gamma-mu, gamma.

With r1=x/y, r2=y/q, q=lambda-p the system is the 3-D Lotka-Volterra cyclic chain r1'=r1(lambda+1-r1-q), r2'=r2(mu-1+r1-r2), q'=q(r2-mu). The adjoint ratio solves eta''+(3eta+2-mu)eta'+f(eta)=x; the chemical ratio y/q solves the same equation with forcing x(A+p)/(lambda-p).

No vector supersolution of the form G = M(t)(c1 x, c2 y, c3 q), with M any positive periodic scalar and c_i constants, exists on any cycle with k > k_H (kills all monomial ansätze x^a y^b q^c). Proof: average the three inequalities using the LV means <x/y>=1, <y/q>=mu, <q>=lambda.

Gauss map injectivity: distinct points of cycles (or E) at the same parameters have distinct (eta,zeta); each cycle is a simple closed curve in the (eta,zeta) plane, clockwise in the Liénard plane (eta, sigma=zeta+eta+eta^2/2) where eta'=sigma-G(eta), sigma'=x-f(eta).

Massera identity: (p^2-Up')' = (eta-mu)(p^2-Up') + pK on every cycle; where p^2-Up'>0 this gives lambda_c = -<pK/(p^2-Up')>. Identity is exact (sympy); positivity of p^2-Up' is observed on nine cycles, not proved.

On W^u(E) the crest return map P1 (coordinate u=U_crest) has P1(u)/u strictly decreasing and P1' decreasing, for mu in {0.02,...,1}, rho in {1.05,...,10} (sampled on crest sequences only). If true on the whole attractor, uniqueness follows. Not monotone in coordinates e^u-1 or y-k.

Pointwise equal-U mirror comparison K_+/omega1_+ >= K_-/omega1_- (upper vs lower arc) is false: the bracket is negative on essentially all of 0<U<U_max. Componentwise concavity of the 2-D crest map in (U, y-k) also fails near Hopf at O(h), by the paper's Theorem 7.1 formulas.

result.obstruction: The weak transverse direction is the second direction of the backward cooperative structure, so its adjoint Psi = z' x v_s has sign-changing components. Every sign-definite object available (supporting planes, K, W, Hölder/Kingman log-convexity, LV averaging) controls only the Perron direction or gives lower bounds on gamma. An upper bound gamma < A needs a positive test function, and every commutator, scaling, fold-type, spectral or duality route I tried reduces to brief 3(e)/3(d). Near Hopf the required sign is an O(h^2) effect under O(h) sign-changing terms (integrand pK/(p^2-Up') is cubic to leading order); at large amplitude stability comes from a different mechanism (x near 0 most of the period). Fold-type exclusion also fails as a strategy: concavity of P1 means any fold would be of birth type, so no 'death-only' argument can close without large-k uniqueness.
